notes:
Prospect summary: Linwood builds an in-product analytics assistant for B2B SaaS customers (help center + in-app insights). Mid-market org with 600 employees; product team owns roadmap. They want to evaluate Hosted API first to accelerate POC, then move to Dedicated if unit economics justify it. Key constraints: EU data residency for a subset of customers, SOC2/KMS, and SSO for internal admin access.

Takeaways from discovery & cost workshop: 
- Workload profile: chat-first (short prompt/short response, avg tokens per request ~ 80), embeddings for search (batched offline ingestion + real-time small-batch), occasional long summarization jobs (1000-2000 tokens). Expected concurrency: 30-50 qps peak for chat during feature rollouts.
- Latency targets: p95 < 200ms for interactive chat, p95 < 1s acceptable for long summaries. Cost sensitivity: high; unit cost per chat session must be < $0.003 to justify scale across freemium tiers.
- Model preference: open/efficient models (Redwood-verified LLaMA variants or similar). Want routing fallback: larger model for premium users, smaller quantized model for free tier.

Cost workshop outcomes (03/01):
- Batching: SE recommended adaptive micro-batching for embeddings ingestion; observed 3-4x throughput improvement in test runs at 128-token windows. For chat, continuous batching with low-latency windows (20-50ms) was proposed to keep p95 below 200ms.
- Caching: KV/prefix caching for multi-turn chat showed 25-40% token savings in initial traces (reuses system prompts + repeated intents). Suggested rules: 24-hour ephemeral cache for session prefixes, retention controls for privacy.
- Quantization profiles: Ran tests with int8 and 4-bit Q4 variants. Results: Q4 reduced GPU memory and increased batch capacity ~2.8x with small quality delta on short chat; int8 gave stable latency but less memory savings. Team is comfortable testing Q4 for non-premium traffic, reserve float or int8 for premium queries.
- Unit economics model: Marcus built a spreadsheet projecting hosted cost vs Dedicated commit. Break-even bound: at sustained 12M tokens/month with the projected committed discount, Dedicated becomes 25-40% cheaper. Current POC throughput indicates ramp to that level within 9-12 months if adoption goes as forecasted.

Risks & questions captured: "Procurement wants guaranteed cost per-token before signing"; "Legal needs data residency appendix for EU"; "Product team wants A/B rollback if quality drops after quantization".

POC specifics: Hosted API test harness instrumented via Redwood telemetry hooks; events being tracked: tokens_in, tokens_out, p50/p95 latency, model_version, quant_profile, cache_hit_rate. Two-week POC objectives: validate p95 < 200ms on Hosted with micro-batching and Q4 for free tier; confirm 30% cost saving via caching + batching; produce a Dedicated pricing term sheet if projections meet break-even.

AE notes / quotes: "Happy with demo speed. Need clearer pricing path to commit — procurement wants committed ARR for discount." SE note: "Q4 looks promising for embeddings + free-tier chat; keep premium on int8/float for safety."

Next steps: finish POC telemetry (due 2026-03-12), run canonical cost-per-session calc, supply Dedicated term sheet and SOW draft, coordinate legal on data residency appendix.
